title: Scene
summary: One illustrated place full of things to find, name and place.
description: Words for the things in a place, learnt where they are: in one drawing of a kitchen, a market stall or a station.

requirements.text: Until its scene is ready, a scene lesson is practised as a words lesson over its things.
When a scene has a thing new to the learner, the lesson opens with the whole scene to explore, where tapping a thing says its name.
The learner finds a thing in the picture by its name, and names a thing that lights up by choosing among the scene's other things.
In a scene lesson of medium or high complexity, a thing that has come back at least twice is named by typing it.
A thing the vision model did not find in the picture is practised as in a words lesson.
A session asks at most three “Where is it?” cards about the scene, in turn a sentence to judge true or false against the picture and a sentence with the place left out to choose.
A “Where is it?” sentence the picture does not bear out is never asked.
